precepts.text: I made a covenant with mine eyes; why then should I think upon a maid? How do you fix it? You have to control what you view. You have to control what you desire. Seeing a beautiful woman does not mean you should think lustfully about her. Especially you married men: you should have a covenant with your eyes with your wife.
precepts.point: Pornography and private sin. Whosoever looketh on a woman to lust after her hath committed adultery with her already in his heart. A lot of you brothers and sisters be doing that: scrolling until something catches your eye, then down the rabbit hole, not caring about any consequences, fully convinced and convicted in your sin.

note.label: Satan's Kiss To Your Demise

precepts.why:
Matthew 5:28 says whosoever looks on a woman to lust after her “hath committed adultery with her already in his heart.” A lot of you brothers do that, and a lot of you sisters do that. You're scrolling down, you see something that catches your eye, and next thing you know you are going down the rabbit hole, full-fledged, not caring about no consequences, fully convinced and convicted in your sin. How do you fix that? Job 31.

“I made a covenant with mine eyes”. You have to control what you view. You have to control what you desire. “why then should I think upon a maid?” I should not be thinking lustfully upon a maid. Because you see a beautiful woman doesn't mean you should think lustfully about that sister; you made a covenant with your eyes. Especially you married men: you should have a covenant with your eyes with your wife. Why should I even think about it?

“For what portion of God is there from above? and what inheritance of the Almighty from on high?” The one who looks to lust has already committed adultery in his heart, and what portion does he have from God then, what inheritance from the Almighty? Read on and Job answers: “Is not destruction to the wicked?”

That is how the private sin of pornography is fought: not after the eye has wandered, but by making the covenant beforehand, so that the looking that leads to adultery in the heart never begins.

precepts.text: I made a covenant with mine eyes; why then should I think upon a maid? Job had to make a covenant: if it comes into my eyesight, I turn away. Netflix keeps it moving to hold your eyes, because the eyes are the portal to the vessel. Psalms 101:3: I will set no wicked thing before mine eyes. Train your eyes to click past the enticing scene, and leave the conversation when the gossip starts, because three seconds of it will taint you.
precepts.point: The brain stores everything: a random song from years ago surfaces because it is saved in long-term memory, the way your stuff never really leaves the internet. What you put into your vessel determines what comes out, and often we do not realize we are being controlled; you were made in a factory called America and those are not your words. The only way to break the code is to reprogram and recode.

note.label: Power Under Control: Food, Sex & Self-Mastery

precepts.why:
“I made a covenant with mine eyes; why then should I think upon a maid?” Job had to literally make a covenant: I'm not going to watch that, and if it gets within my eyesight, I got to turn away. I got to train my eyes to look away.

That is the three-second rule. The eyes are input. If you let yourself look at something for more than three seconds, it goes into your working memory, your short-term memory; keep looking at it and you are programming yourself into long-term memory. Turn away within three seconds and it doesn't have time to work within your memory. That is why TikTok gives you three seconds to capture somebody's attention, and why Netflix keeps it moving: once they have your attention through your eyes, they have you. Our eyes are the portal to take control over your vessel.

The algorithm is a reflection of you. Your searches and your scrolls tell who you are, what makes you sad, what makes you mad, what music you play when you're angry. So when you say the algorithm got you, it's not them getting you. It's you, manifested on a screen. The devil don't make you do anything you don't want to do.

David said the same: “I will set no wicked thing before mine eyes.” Train your eyes. If a show is full of action but something enticing comes on that goes against your values and your struggles, turn it off, click by. If you hear gossip or something negative, leave the conversation, because three seconds of listening will taint you, and three seconds of something negatively influencing you will control you.

note.label: Genesis 3: The Craftiness of Your Enemy

precepts.why:
“If I covered my transgressions as Adam, by hiding mine iniquity in my bosom”. Adam covered his transgressions. That is what the fig leaves are.

Remember this is an illustrated story. When “they sewed fig leaves together, and made themselves aprons”, the fig leaves and aprons represent them trying to cover their transgressions, hiding their iniquity as Adam did.

precepts.text: Is not destruction to the wicked? Doth not he see my ways and count all my steps?
precepts.point: The truth is the opposite: when Job had his riches he dealt righteously, helped people, taught people, and was looked up to like an elder in the city.

note.label: Job 22: Acquaint Now Thyself With Him

precepts.why:
“Is not destruction to the wicked? and a strange punishment to the workers of iniquity? Doth not he see my ways, and count all my steps?” Job knows destruction is to the wicked, and he knows the Most High sees his ways and counts all his steps. So he does not fear the accounting Eliphaz tries to lay on him.

Eliphaz accuses him of taking a pledge from his brother for naught, stripping the naked of their clothing, withholding water from the weary and bread from the hungry, sending widows away empty, and breaking the arms of the fatherless, and says that is why snares are round about him. But the Lord was only trying him. The truth is the opposite: when Job had his riches he dealt righteously, helped people, taught people, and was looked up to like an elder in the city, and God counted every one of those steps.

precepts.text: If Job walked with vanity or deceit, let another eat what he sowed and his offspring be rooted out.
precepts.point: The truth is the opposite: when Job had his riches he dealt righteously, helped people, taught people, and was looked up to like an elder in the city.

note.label: Job 22: Acquaint Now Thyself With Him

precepts.why:
Job answers the accusation with his own oath: “If I have walked with vanity, or if my foot hath hasted to deceit; Let me be weighed in an even balance, that God may know mine integrity.” “If my step hath turned out of the way, and mine heart walked after mine eyes, and if any blot hath cleaved to mine hands; Then let me sow, and let another eat; yea, let my offspring be rooted out.” If Job walked with vanity or deceit, let another eat what he sowed and his offspring be rooted out.

That is not the answer of a man who stripped the naked of their clothing and withheld bread from the hungry, as Eliphaz claims. Eliphaz says Job's suffering proves Job was sinning, but the Lord was only trying him. When Job had his riches he dealt righteously, helped people, taught people, and was looked up to like an elder in the city, and he asks to be weighed in an even balance to prove it.

precepts.text: If Job's heart was deceived by a woman or he laid wait at his neighbor's door, let his wife grind unto another; Job shows he dealt righteously.
precepts.point: The truth is the opposite: when Job had his riches he dealt righteously, helped people, taught people, and was looked up to like an elder in the city.

note.label: Job 22: Acquaint Now Thyself With Him

precepts.why:
“If mine heart have been deceived by a woman, or if I have laid wait at my neighbour’s door; Then let my wife grind unto another, and let others bow down upon her.” If Job's heart was deceived by a woman or he laid wait at his neighbor's door, let his wife grind unto another. Job shows he dealt righteously; he lays his own wife on the line against the charge.

So Eliphaz's claim that snares are round about Job and sudden fear troubles him because he sent widows away empty and broke the arms of the fatherless does not stand. Eliphaz claims Job's suffering proves Job was sinning, but the Lord was only trying him. The truth is the opposite: when Job had his riches he dealt righteously, helped people, taught people, and was looked up to like an elder in the city.

precepts.text: The one who commits adultery with another man's wife lacks understanding and destroys his own soul; jealousy is the rage of a man and he will not spare in the day of vengeance.
precepts.point: If his heart was deceived by a woman or he laid wait at his neighbor's door, then let his wife grind unto another and let others bow down upon her. Job is saying if he committed adultery let the same come back on him, for this is a heinous crime, a fire that consumeth to destruction and would root out all his increase.

note.label: Job 31: The Words Of Job Are Ended

precepts.why:
Job says, “If mine heart have been deceived by a woman, or if I have laid wait at my neighbour’s door; Then let my wife grind unto another, and let others bow down upon her.” If he committed adultery, let the same come back on him, “For this is an heinous crime; yea, it is an iniquity to be punished by the judges.”

Proverbs shows how heinous: “So he that goeth in to his neighbour’s wife; whosoever toucheth her shall not be innocent.” Men do not despise a thief who steals to satisfy his soul when he is hungry, and if he is found he restores sevenfold. “But whoso committeth adultery with a woman lacketh understanding: he that doeth it destroyeth his own soul. A wound and dishonour shall he get; and his reproach shall not be wiped away.”

“For jealousy is the rage of a man: therefore he will not spare in the day of vengeance. He will not regard any ransom; neither will he rest content, though thou givest many gifts.” The punishment of adultery is severe, and there is not much a man can do if he finds it out. That is why a lot of men die nowadays sleeping with other men's wives, and a lot of people are in jail behind one. It is a fire that consumeth to destruction and would root out all a man's increase.
